key_insight: Microscopic compositional impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films act as degradation nucleation sites, and they can be rapidly detected with microscopy plus machine-learning image analysis.
engineering_relevance: This provides a fast, non-invasive pre-screening tool for stability control in scalable perovskite solar-cell manufacturing and tandem-device qualification.
method: Nano-FTIR, high-resolution optical microscopy, and scanning probe techniques chemically identified impurity regions.
Photo-stress testing mapped where degradation begins at impurity–perovskite interfaces.
Reflected-light microscopy with ML-supported image analysis enabled seconds-scale impurity detection and quantification.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that films with higher impurity density showed faster early degradation, and degradation tracking revealed coupled photo- and thermo-chemical instability.
watch_item: The diagnostic workflow is chemically validated, but real-world deployment may require calibration across film compositions, imaging setups, and manufacturing variability.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
